question: Who will win the 2026 U.S. Senate election in Maine — Republican incumbent Susan Collins or Democrat Graham Platner?
title: Maine U.S. Senate — Collins vs. Platner
resolution: Resolves to the winner of the Maine U.S. Senate general election on Nov 3, 2026 (ranked-choice tabulation if no candidate exceeds 50% in the first round).

consensus.headline_case: This is a near-toss-up that tilts, but only slightly, toward a Democratic pickup — below where the money sits. The three exact-question markets cluster at Democrat ~57-61%, and two independent reads agree: the outside view (split-state seats went 4 of 4 to the presidential-lean party in 2024; the president's party lost Senate seats in 13 of 20 midterms) and the driver read (an anti-GOP headwind on the lone incumbent-party senator in a state that voted ~9 points Democratic). We sit the modal Platner win at 37-47%, not the market's ~59%, because the head-to-head polls are a tie (mean ~D+1), not a lead — the tilt is pricing Maine's presidential lean, which Collins has personally detached from before. Add Platner's live candidate-quality risk as a subtractor the market underweights, and the summed Collins-survival paths (~38-56%) make it closer to a coin flip than the tape implies.
consensus.why_over_runner_up: The environment-driven Platner win edges the Collins hold because the fundamentals — presidential lean, midterm punishment on the incumbent party, Collins's record-low ~38% approval — all push one way, and the market agrees. Collins-survival rests on a genuine but 1-of-1 personal escape (her +17.5-point 2020 ticket-split), which caps rather than anchors the scenario; mismatch survival is only ~5-15%.
consensus.dissent: The Quant's case is the strongest surviving counter: the market and the polls disagree by ~15 points, and that gap is the whole ballgame. If the near-tied head-to-head polls (Fox R+3, NYT/Siena D+2, Quantus D+1, UMass D+5) are the truer signal and the market is merely pricing presidential lean, then a senator who has already outrun her state's lean by 17.5 points sits at roughly a coin flip she can win — not the underdog the ~59% price makes her.

profiles.name: The Market Reader
profiles.criterion: Sides with the price the sharpest, deepest, most liquid markets have settled on.
profiles.blurb: The deepest book has spoken. Polymarket ran ~$619K and settled Democrat ~56%. Kalshi says D ~58-61. Manifold says 57.7. Three books, one direction. I take the price.
profiles.evidence: Three exact-question markets cluster Democrat ~57-61%; Polymarket ~56% on ~$619K, the deepest liquidity on the question.

profiles.name: The Quant
profiles.criterion: Trusts simulation models and structured decompositions over recency and sentiment.
profiles.blurb: The market and the polls disagree by fifteen points, and I decline to look away from that. The head-to-head mean is D+1 — a tie — while the price says D+59. That wedge is presidential lean, and this particular senator has already unhitched herself from it by 17.5 points once. Decompose it honestly and the hold is a live 34%, not the market's implied 42.
profiles.evidence: ~15-point market-vs-poll wedge (mean ~D+1); Collins's +17.5-point 2020 personal ticket-split detaches her from the state's lean.

profiles.name: The Historian
profiles.criterion: Counted reference-class base rates and venue history.
profiles.blurb: Count them, the seasons of the incumbent party in the off-year: thirteen midterms of twenty since 1934 gave up their Senate seats, the average toll near four. Count the mismatch states of 2024: four of four bent to the presidential lean, none the other way. The ledger reads one direction, and Maine leans nine points blue. The environment does not spare the lone senator of the party in power.
profiles.evidence: President's party lost Senate seats in 13 of 20 midterms; 2024 split-state seats went 4 of 4 to the presidential-lean party.

profiles.name: The Path Reader
profiles.criterion: Ignores reputation; reads the actual route, mechanism, and path dependence.
profiles.blurb: Follow the route, not the name. The lean is D+9. The polls sit at D+1. Under ranked choice the second round consolidates the Democratic-plus-independent majority. Platner wins narrow, despite his scandals, not because of them. Low single digits. That is the path.
profiles.evidence: Maine's ~9-point Democratic presidential lean plus RCV second-round consolidation of a D-leaning electorate produces a narrow Platner margin.

profiles.name: The Talisman
profiles.criterion: Elite individual actors, motivation, proven leadership.
profiles.blurb: I sing the one who has stood five campaigns and bends the state to her own name. In 2020 she walked seventeen and a half points past her party's fate, won by 8.6 as the top of the ticket fell by nine. In 2008 she took 61 while the state went the other way. The seniority, the chair, the closing war chest of $9.7 million against $2.2 — the proven figure gathers the late undecided to herself. I back the incumbent's own gravity.
profiles.evidence: Collins's +17.5-point 2020 split and 61% 2008 win; ~$9.7M cash-on-hand vs Platner's ~$2.2M for the closing air war.

profiles.name: The Contrarian
profiles.criterion: Favorites usually fail; hunts the underpriced live path.
profiles.blurb: Everyone is pricing the environment and no one is pricing the tattoo. Note the class: flawed nominees in winnable seats — Akin, Mourdock, Walker, Masters, Bolduc — forfeited roughly five of five once the scandal became the frame. Note also that the price already twitched when the sexting story broke. A 9-17% clear Collins win on a fresh October beat is the one live path the tape is quietly leaving on the table.
profiles.evidence: Flawed-nominee reference class forfeited ~5/5 winnable seats; Platner's market odds already dropped during the sexting scandal.

profiles.name: The Prophet
profiles.criterion: Backs the fated, story-shaped outcome the events seem to be scripting — however long the odds.
profiles.blurb: Read the shape of it and tell me this ending is not already written. Once before, in 2020, not one of fifteen public polls showed her ahead, and she won anyway by 8.6 — the escape the models could not see coming. Now the challenger arrives pre-damaged, handing the ticket-splitters their permission to come home, and the hard-to-poll rural county waits again to be undercounted as it was then. The story has rehearsed this scene. The fifth term is the fated close, and the omens — the 1-of-1 escape, the flawed rival, the polling miss lying in wait — all point to the senator surviving.
profiles.evidence: 0 of ~15 public polls showed her leading in 2020 yet she won +8.6; the 2020 rural polling-miss mechanism recurs with a flawed challenger supplying a permission structure.

base_rates.text: 2024 split-state Senate seats all went to the party matching the state's presidential lean (AZ/MI/NV/WI), 0 the other way — favors Platner in D-leaning Maine, though none of those winners was scandal-damaged.
The president's party lost Senate seats in 13 of 20 midterms since 1934 (~65%, avg ~3.5-4 seats). The backlash lands on the incumbent-party senator — Collins.
Presidential-Senate mismatch survival is rare and shrinking (~2 cases across 2020-2022; Collins was 1 of ~35 in 2020). Caps the Collins-hold scenario as the exception, not the rule.
Collins's personal ticket-split in 2020 — won by +8.6 while Trump lost Maine ~9, with 0 of ~15 polls showing her ahead. A 1-of-1 escape that caps rather than anchors her brand case.

Multi-decade Senate incumbent reelection rate; 2022 saw 0 of ~35 incumbents lose. An incumbency floor under Collins, blunted because recent losses cluster on the party carrying the midterm-mood deficit.

Clearly flawed nominees (Akin, Mourdock, Walker, Masters, Bolduc) forfeited winnable seats once a scandal became the defining frame — the mechanism that could hand Collins a race the fundamentals deny her.

Mean of post-primary head-to-head Maine polls (Fox R+3, NYT/Siena D+2, Quantus D+1, UMass D+5) — a statistical tie versus exact-question markets at D ~57-61%; the ~15-point wedge is the central disputed quantity.

triggers: Post-Labor-Day live-caller Maine polling: a stable Platner lead greater than 5 points across multiple polls confirms the environment-Platner path and guts the Collins-hold case; head-to-head staying within a few points sustains the toss-up and the polls-truer read.

Exact-question market drift from the 2026-07-03 D~57-61% anchor: a sustained move above D>65% forces the Collins-hold paths down; a move below D<50% forces the environment scenario down and could flip the modal read toward Collins.

Trump national approval and the generic ballot: recovery above ~44% approval or a generic ballot returning to even by October compresses the Democratic edge and helps Collins; further decline (Trump toward the low-30s, generic at least D+6 sustained) strengthens the Platner and blue-wave paths.

A new or corroborated Platner scandal — especially corroboration of the NYT abuse allegations or a defining October frame — raises the implosion scenario and pulls mass from the Democratic paths; the controversies receding from coverage by mid-October weakens the flawed-challenger drag and helps Platner.

National Democratic committee spending in Maine: pulling or cancelling ad reservations signals they have written Platner off (implosion up); reaffirming or increasing late spending signals they have not (implosion down).
A macro shock (recession call, major national crisis) or a candidate health/withdrawal event activates the structural-surprise tail and would require a full re-forecast.

method_note: Anchored on three exact-question markets (Polymarket ~$619K D~56%; Kalshi D~58-61%; Manifold D~57.7%; pulled 2026-07-03). Two reads agreed on direction: the counted outside view (2024 mismatches 4 of 4 to the presidential-lean party) and the driver read (anti-GOP headwind on the lone incumbent-party senator in a D+9 state). The unrefuted objection — the market prices presidential lean, not the near-tied polls (mean ~D+1) — pulls the call below the market. Horizon: through Nov 3, 2026.
honesty_note: This tilts toward a Platner pickup, but the modal scenario sits at only 37-47% — meaning it is more likely than not that this exact scenario does NOT happen. The summed Collins-survival paths (~38-56%) are competitive with it. Treat this as a genuine coin flip tilted slightly below the market, not a confident Democratic call; the decisive evidence is still in the future.
